name_en: Jaw width relative to cheekbone width
name_vi: Chiều rộng xương hàm so với gò má
what_it_controls: The taper of the lower face. Low values read as a narrow jaw, values near 1.0 as a square one
failure_when_wrong: This is the parameter image models drift most under a beauty prompt, always toward a narrower jaw. If it is not written down it will not survive ten generations
prompt_phrasing: jaw width about three quarters of cheekbone width
source: No primary source found for the skeletal landmark names gonion and zygion. Wikipedia's craniofacial anthropometry entry redirects to a history of scientific racism and carries no landmark list, so it was not used. FISWG expresses cheek width as a relative descriptor instead and that is the safer framing. FISWG Facial Image Comparison Feature List for Morphological Analysis v2.0 2018-09-11, https://www.fiswg.org/documents/ - section 3.4 defines every distance as relative to face width or height, never absolute

name_vi: Khoảng cách từ chân mày đến mí
what_it_controls: How much lid space is visible. This is the surface every eyeshadow look in makeup-looks.csv is painted on, so the look and the space have to be specified together
failure_when_wrong: A graphic editorial eye specified onto a shallow lid comes back either flattened or with the brow relocated
prompt_phrasing: moderate visible lid space between brow and lash line
source: Composed from two relative distances for this skill. No standard term found for the ratio. The FISWG practice of stating a distance relative to the face rather than in millimetres is what is borrowed. FISWG Facial Image Comparison Feature List for Morphological Analysis v2.0 2018-09-11, https://www.fiswg.org/documents/ - section 3.4 defines every distance as relative to face width or height, never absolute

name_vi: Độ nghiêng trục mắt
what_it_controls: The angle of the line from inner to outer eye corner. It sets whether the eye reads upturned or downturned, which is most of what people mean by expression at rest
failure_when_wrong: Left unspecified, a generator will fluctuate between frames and the same person will read alternately sharp and sleepy
prompt_phrasing: slightly upturned outer eye corners, about four degrees
source: Canthus, the corner where upper and lower eyelids meet; endocanthion and exocanthion are the medial and lateral cephalometric landmarks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canthus. No published range found for the tilt angle, so the domain here is an input range only

name_vi: Một nét bất đối xứng hoặc dấu riêng
unit: named location and size in mm-equivalent
input_domain: exactly one, stated with a side
what_it_controls: The thing that makes the face a person rather than an average. A mole above the left jaw, a slightly lower right brow, one crooked lower incisor
failure_when_wrong: A perfectly symmetric face is the strongest single tell of generated imagery, and it is also unownable - it is the average of the training set, so it belongs to nobody and resembles everybody
prompt_phrasing: small mole two centimetres above the left jaw line, right brow sitting marginally lower
source: This skill's own rule, from slop-tells.csv on generated-face symmetry. Bridgman's independent statement of why symmetry is wrong is structural rather than aesthetic: the masses are balanced symmetrically over each other rarely in life and in action never. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft

name_vi: Tỷ lệ dài trên rộng của khuôn mặt
what_it_controls: Whether the face reads long or wide at any crop. It is the single parameter that survives being resized to a 40px avatar, so it does more identity work than any feature
failure_when_wrong: Drift here is what makes a virtual model look like a different person between two posts while every individual feature still matches
prompt_phrasing: face length to cheekbone width about 1.40 to 1
source: Expressed as a relative distance rather than a measurement, which is FISWG practice. FISWG Facial Image Comparison Feature List for Morphological Analysis v2.0 2018-09-11, https://www.fiswg.org/documents/ - section 3.4 defines every distance as relative to face width or height, never absolute. FISWG's own caution is that photoanthropometry should not be used for identification at all; the vocabulary is borrowed for description, not for identifying anyone

name_vi: Phân chia ba phần khuôn mặt
what_it_controls: Where the brow line and the nose base fall down the face. Shifting weight into the lower third reads as a longer chin; into the upper third as a higher hairline
failure_when_wrong: A face specified only by features and never by its thirds is a face the model will re-proportion every render
prompt_phrasing: brow, nose base and chin dividing the face into roughly equal thirds
source: Hairline to nasal root, nasal root to nasal base, nasal base to chin as three equal parts. FISWG figure 2, canon A, after Vegter and Hage 2000, Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery 106(5):1090-1096

name_en: Forehead height as share of face length
name_vi: Chiều cao trán trên chiều dài mặt
what_it_controls: Where the hairline sits, which is the parameter a fringe hides. Lock it anyway, because the fringe is styling and will change
failure_when_wrong: A character locked only in a fringed hairstyle has no defined face above the brow, and the first swept-back styling reveals a different person
prompt_phrasing: hairline at roughly a third of the face length
source: Trichion, the anterior hairline at the midline. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/. The thirds that place it are FISWG figure 2, canon A, after Vegter and Hage 2000, Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery 106(5):1090-1096

name_en: Eye spacing relative to face width
name_vi: Khoảng cách hai mắt so với bề rộng mặt
what_it_controls: How far apart the eyes sit. Together with the facial index it accounts for most of the resemblance a viewer registers before they can name a single feature
failure_when_wrong: The most common cause of a virtual model that is recognisable in close-up and a stranger at half-body distance
prompt_phrasing: eye spacing a little under half the face width
source: FISWG lists nose and mouth widths relative to interpupillary distance among its ratio descriptors. FISWG Facial Image Comparison Feature List for Morphological Analysis v2.0 2018-09-11, https://www.fiswg.org/documents/ - section 3.4 defines every distance as relative to face width or height, never absolute. Canon C, intercanthal distance equals one eye width, is the classical form of the same relation: FISWG figure 2, canon A, after Vegter and Hage 2000, Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery 106(5):1090-1096

name_en: Nose width relative to mouth width
name_vi: Bề rộng mũi so với bề rộng miệng
what_it_controls: The relationship between the two features that sit on the same vertical axis, which is what makes the centre of the face read as one structure rather than two
failure_when_wrong: Specify the nose and the mouth separately and they will each be plausible and jointly wrong
prompt_phrasing: nose width about seven tenths of mouth width
source: Named explicitly in the FISWG face composition descriptors. FISWG Facial Image Comparison Feature List for Morphological Analysis v2.0 2018-09-11, https://www.fiswg.org/documents/ - section 3.4 defines every distance as relative to face width or height, never absolute

name_en: Philtrum length as share of lower third
name_vi: Chiều dài nhân trung trên phần ba dưới
what_it_controls: The distance from nose base to upper lip. Small changes here move the whole apparent age and are almost never specified, which is why they drift
failure_when_wrong: Unspecified, this is where a generator quietly ages or de-ages a locked character between campaigns
prompt_phrasing: short philtrum, under a quarter of the lower face
source: Philtrum, the vertical indentation of the upper lip running from the nasal septum to the tubercle. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philtrum. Subnasale is where the columella merges with the upper lip. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/

name_vi: Tỷ lệ môi trên và môi dưới
what_it_controls: The visible red of the upper lip against the lower. This is the parameter an overlined-lip makeup look changes, so lock it bare and let the makeup row do the styling
failure_when_wrong: Confusing this with the makeup means the model's mouth changes shape every time the campaign changes lipstick
prompt_phrasing: lower lip about one and a half times the upper
source: Labrale superioris and inferioris are the vermilion borders of the upper and lower lip. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/. No published ratio found, so the domain is an input range

name_en: Hand length relative to face length
name_vi: Chiều dài bàn tay so với mặt
what_it_controls: Hand scale. The canon is that a hand is as long as the face, which is larger than almost anyone estimates, and stating it is what stops the hands arriving small
failure_when_wrong: Undersized hands are the commonest structural error in both drawing and generation, and the instruction sources describe it as a budget failure rather than a care failure: hands are the last form added and therefore the first degraded. Stating the ratio moves them out of the leftover budget
prompt_phrasing: hands as long as the face, at true scale
source: Hands as long as the face. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions. Bridgman's structure for the hand is two masses, the hand proper and the thumb, with the knuckles on one arc concentric around the base of the thumb and the second knuckle largest and highest. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft

name_en: Leg length as share of stature
name_vi: Tỷ lệ chân trên tổng chiều cao
what_it_controls: Where the waist sits in the frame, which decides where a full-body composition can be cropped without cutting the figure at a joint
failure_when_wrong: Unspecified, it interacts with the head-unit count and the figure comes back elongated below the waist only - the specific distortion that reads as an AI fashion image
prompt_phrasing: legs slightly under half the total height
source: The vertical midpoint of a standing figure is the line between the greater trochanters, just above the pubic arch, not the waist. Legs measured floor to crotch run 3.5 to 4 heads, arms about 3 heads. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions

name_vi: Chiều dài cổ theo đầu
what_it_controls: The gap between jaw and shoulder line. It decides whether a chin-forward pose is available at all, and whether a high collar covers the whole neck
failure_when_wrong: A short neck plus a chin-elevation instruction produces the compressed jaw that gets read as a bad render rather than a bad pose
prompt_phrasing: neck a little over a third of a head height
source: No source found stating neck length in head units. The sourced neck geometry is the mentocervical angle, which is carried by the chin row. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/

name_vi: Dáng đứng mặc định
unit: degrees of thoracic lean and shoulder drop
what_it_controls: How the person stands when not posing. A consistent small asymmetry is what makes a series of frames read as one human being
failure_when_wrong: Perfect posture in every frame is the second-strongest generated-image tell after facial symmetry
prompt_phrasing: weight settled, right shoulder marginally lower, very slight forward lean
source: Head, chest and pelvis are three unchanging masses whose relations are limited to three planes: bent forward and back, twisted, tilted, and almost invariably all three are present to different degrees. Balanced symmetrically over each other rarely in life, in action never. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft

name_en: Shoulder to hip lateral width ratio
name_vi: Tỷ lệ bề rộng vai trên hông
what_it_controls: The head-on width of the figure at the two places a silhouette is read. It is the one axis on this sheet with a published mean, standard deviation and observed range behind it rather than an input domain somebody chose
failure_when_wrong: Pushed past the observed range this is the axis that reads as a generated body rather than a photographed one, because it exceeds what the measured distribution contains and the viewer has seen thousands of real ones
prompt_phrasing: shoulders about 1.05 times hip width, head on
source: Head-on lateral width ratio, shoulders to hips, Hughes and Gallup 2003 as reported in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions: men 1.18 with a standard deviation of 0.071 and an observed range of 1.03 to 1.40; women 1.03, standard deviation 0.066, range 0.90 to 1.22

name_vi: Tỷ lệ vai trên eo
what_it_controls: Torso taper. With shoulder width it fully specifies the upper body outline, which is what apparel photography is actually selling
failure_when_wrong: Describing a build with an adjective instead of this ratio is how a clothing brand ends up with a model whose proportions differ between the flat-lay frame and the on-model frame
prompt_phrasing: modest taper from shoulder to waist, about 1.3 to 1
source: No measured distribution found for a shoulder-to-waist ratio. The adjacent measured span is shoulder to hip, which is a different landmark and has its own row. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions

name_vi: Bề rộng vai theo đầu
what_it_controls: Frame width at the top of the figure, which sets how the garment hangs and how much of the background the silhouette covers
failure_when_wrong: Left open, this is the axis a generator moves to make a figure read as authoritative or delicate, so the same character changes build with the mood of the prompt
prompt_phrasing: shoulders about two head widths across
source: No source found stating shoulder width in head units. The sourced lateral measure is a shoulder-to-hip width ratio, which is carried by its own row. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions

name_vi: Chiều cao tính theo số đầu
what_it_controls: Overall proportion without ever stating a height in centimetres, which is what makes the sheet work at any crop and in any country
failure_when_wrong: Fashion illustration convention runs to 8.5 or 9 heads and an image model has absorbed that. Unspecified, a full-body frame will drift toward illustration proportions and stop matching the half-body frames
prompt_phrasing: natural proportions, about seven and a half head heights
source: The head as the unit of measurement, credited to Polykleitos. An average adult is 7.5 heads, the conventional ideal figure 8, the heroic figure 8.5, used for superhuman power. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_proportions

name_en: Negative space between arm and torso
name_vi: Khoảng trống giữa tay và thân
what_it_controls: Whether background is visible between the upper arm and the waist. A visible gap separates the arm from the body and is what makes a waist readable at all
failure_when_wrong: Zero gap fuses arm and torso into one mass, so the figure widens and the waist disappears. It is the commonest reason a good pose photographs badly, and it is invisible to the person posing
prompt_phrasing: clear gap of background visible between the upper arm and the waist
source: The spaces between the arms and body, or legs and ground or chair. Useful for correcting proportions, which is why closing the gap removes information rather than only looking crowded. https://lifemodelssociety.org/2021/08/04/common-art-life-modelling-terms/. Bridgman gives the structural reason: masses of about the same size or proportion are conceived not as masses but as one mass, and the effective conception is wedging one into another. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft

name_vi: Độ hạ nâng của cằm
unit: degrees from the Frankfort horizontal, signed
what_it_controls: Pitch of the head. Slightly down defines the jaw line and shortens the nose; up exposes the underside of the jaw and the nostrils
failure_when_wrong: A dropped chin plus a low camera is the pairing that produces a double chin in an otherwise correct frame. This parameter is meaningless without the camera height beside it
prompt_phrasing: chin lowered about three degrees, jaw line held long
source: Pitch is measured against the Frankfort horizontal, which is what makes it a number rather than an impression. Frankfort horizontal plane, superior external auditory canal to inferior infraorbital rim, approximated in a photograph as superior tragus to the lower eyelid and cheek junction. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/. The chin landmarks are menton, the lowest point, pogonion, the most anterior point in profile, and the cervical point; the mentocervical angle across that transition is reported at 80 to 95 degrees. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/

name_vi: Độ lệch hướng nhìn so với ống kính
what_it_controls: Whether the subject looks into the lens. Zero is address, and it is the choice that makes a frame feel spoken to the viewer; off-axis needs a reason in frame or it reads as avoidance
failure_when_wrong: Off-axis gaze with nothing for the subject to be looking at is the single most common unforced error in small-brand photography
prompt_phrasing: looking directly into the lens
source: No primary source found for a gaze-offset convention. The observed rule that an off-axis gaze needs something in frame to be looking at is recorded in reference-observations.csv, ningning-salon-pink-on-pink

name_vi: Cách tạo hình bàn tay
what_it_controls: What the fingers are doing. Fingers relaxed into a slight curl, or in contact with a surface, or closed around an object - never straight and spread
failure_when_wrong: A flat splayed hand shows every finger in full length, which is the pose generators render worst and the one that most often comes back with the wrong finger count. Giving the hand an object to close around removes the failure instead of hoping past it
prompt_phrasing: fingers relaxed and slightly curled, closed around the object
source: The masses of the hand are two, the hand proper and the thumb. The knuckles lie on one arc concentric around the base of the thumb, the second knuckle larger and higher than the rest. The palmar interossei are collectors drawing the fingers toward the middle finger and the dorsal interossei are spreaders drawing away from it, so the fingers move as a fan about the middle finger rather than as five independent sticks. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft

name_en: Working hand height relative to the eyeline
name_vi: Độ cao của tay so với đường mắt
unit: head units above or below eyeline
what_it_controls: Where the occupied hand sits. At the eyeline it becomes a second focal point at the same height as the face; above the crown it outranks the face entirely
failure_when_wrong: Empty hands hanging at the hip is what makes a person look like they are waiting rather than working. Every frame in the four-post salon set has one forearm raised into frame holding something from the set
prompt_phrasing: one forearm raised into frame at eye height, holding the product
source: This skill's own axis, from reference-observations.csv, aespa-kissntell-one-set-four-posts. The independent instruction-source finding is that hands are a budget failure rather than a care failure: in fast studies there is too little time to suggest smaller forms such as hands, and the prescribed fix is to give them their own construction time. https://doctorlib.org/anatomy/classic-human-anatomy-motion/11.html

name_vi: Độ nghiêng đầu
unit: degrees from vertical, head upright on the Frankfort horizontal
what_it_controls: Lateral tilt of the head, independent of rotation. A few degrees reads as attention; past about twelve it becomes a performed cuteness that dates fast
failure_when_wrong: Tilt with no counter-rotation in the shoulders reads as a broken neck rather than a gesture
prompt_phrasing: head tilted about five degrees toward the raised shoulder
source: Tilting is a form bending to the side away from a vertical alignment, measured as the angle between the form's central axis and the vertical. Winslow, Classic Human Anatomy in Motion, https://doctorlib.org/anatomy/classic-human-anatomy-motion/12.html. Head position in a photograph is standardised against the Frankfort horizontal, not against the frame. Frankfort horizontal plane, superior external auditory canal to inferior infraorbital rim, approximated in a photograph as superior tragus to the lower eyelid and cheek junction. Facial Analysis, ENT Secrets ch 60, https://clinicalpub.com/facial-analysis/

name_vi: Độ quay đầu
what_it_controls: Rotation of the head independently of the torso. Full face at 0, three-quarter anywhere from almost frontal to almost profile, profile at 90. Turning the head against the torso is what stops a three-quarter body reading as a person who has simply been rotated
failure_when_wrong: Head yaw locked to torso rotation gives the mannequin turn: every plane of the figure facing the same way, which is the pose a shop dummy holds and no person does
prompt_phrasing: head turned about twenty degrees off full face
source: Full face to profile, with three-quarter anywhere in between, ranging from almost frontal to almost profile. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait_painting

name_en: Counter-rotation between hip line and shoulder line
name_vi: Độ xoay ngược giữa trục hông và trục vai
what_it_controls: This is contrapposto stated as a number. Weight on one leg raises that hip; the shoulder on the same side drops, so the two axes tilt in opposite directions and the spine takes an S
failure_when_wrong: Zero counter-rotation with an off-centre weight is the uncanny standing pose: the hips are doing something the shoulders have not answered
prompt_phrasing: right hip raised, right shoulder dropped, about twelve degrees of opposition
source: In the frontal plane the relation is reciprocal: right hip higher means right shoulder lower, and the reverse. In the axial plane shoulders and arms twist off the axis of hips and legs. First instance conventionally dated to the Kritios Boy, about 480 BCE. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrapposto

name_vi: Đường chuyển động chính
unit: named curve: straight, C, S, reverse-S
what_it_controls: The single curve running from head through the weight-bearing foot that the whole pose is built on. Drawn first in figure instruction, and the reason a pose reads as one gesture and not a set of arranged limbs
failure_when_wrong: Posing limb by limb with no line of action gives a figure that is correct joint by joint and lifeless overall. This is the difference people cannot name when they say a photo looks stiff
prompt_phrasing: a single soft S running from the head down through the standing foot
source: The directional movement of the whole figure within a pose, more organic than the central axis and at times not following it, indicating a sweeping alignment rather than a joint-by-joint one. A strong directional alignment of torso, limbs and head is what creates the illusion of movement in a stationary figure. Winslow, Classic Human Anatomy in Motion, https://doctorlib.org/anatomy/classic-human-anatomy-motion/12.html. The S-curve involves more of the body than contrapposto and guides the eye through the image to the subject at the end of the curve. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-curve_(art)

name_vi: Dáng mở hay dáng đóng
what_it_controls: Whether the limbs are spread with the head up, or curled and compact with limbs crossing and sometimes the face hidden. It decides how much silhouette the frame gets before any other choice is made
failure_when_wrong: A closed pose is not a mistake, but it is named as its own category because crossing limbs and a hidden face are the two things that break legibility. Choosing closed means accepting that overlap has to be resolved by light or colour instead
prompt_phrasing: open pose, arms clear of the body, head up
source: Open pose is arms spread wide and head up. Closed pose is shrunken, curled or compact, limbs often crossing one another and sometimes the face hidden. https://lifemodelssociety.org/2021/08/04/common-art-life-modelling-terms/

name_vi: Kiểm tra tiếp tuyến và chồng chi
input_domain: pass required at wrist, elbow, knee, ankle, crown
what_it_controls: Whether a contour of the figure runs exactly along a background edge, and whether the frame cuts a limb at a joint. Both read as an error even when nothing is wrong with the pose
failure_when_wrong: A frame cropped at the wrist or ankle reads as amputated; a shoulder line coincident with a horizon line flattens the figure into the background
prompt_phrasing: crop between joints, not at them; keep the figure contour off the background edges
source: No primary source found. Searched for teaching sources on tangency and on cropping at the joints; every ranked result was a content-marketing tip list. The nearest sourced substitute describes the same failure structurally: two masses of similar size and proportion merge into one mass. Bridgman, Constructive Anatomy, 1920, https://archive.org/details/constructiveanat00briduoft. The sourced crop conventions name the accepted framings, full-length, half-length, head and shoulders, head only, without prohibiting the others: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait_painting

name_vi: Độ xoay thân so với chính diện
what_it_controls: Frontal at 0, three-quarter near 30 to 45, profile at 90. Three-quarter is the default for a person because it shows two planes of the torso and narrows the silhouette at the same time
failure_when_wrong: Full frontal at 0 reads as an identity document unless the pose is deliberately inert; full profile hides the product side of the body
prompt_phrasing: torso turned about thirty degrees off camera, face returning to the lens
source: Full face, three-quarter and profile as the named head and body views, alongside the crop conventions full-length, half-length, head and shoulders, head only. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrait_painting. Rotation is read off the midline, which has the same alignment as the internal central axis but lies on the surface: the sternum from the front, the vertebral column from the back. Winslow, Classic Human Anatomy in Motion, https://doctorlib.org/anatomy/classic-human-anatomy-motion/12.html

name_vi: Phân bố trọng lượng lên chân trụ
what_it_controls: The root of every standing pose. The leg carrying the weight is the engaged leg and the other is the free leg; moving off 50/50 is what stops a figure reading as a mannequin
failure_when_wrong: Even weight makes a standing figure inert. It is the correct choice only when the styling is doing all the work and stillness is the point
prompt_phrasing: weight on the left leg, right leg relaxed and slightly bent
source: Engaged leg bears the weight and is straight or very slightly bent; free leg is relaxed and slightly bent. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrapposto. The life-model working cue is compression on the weight-bearing side, so the shoulder and hip on that side sit closer together, which is checkable left against right. https://lifemodelssociety.org/2021/08/04/common-art-life-modelling-terms/

name_en: Camera height relative to the subject eyeline
name_vi: Độ cao máy so với đường mắt
what_it_controls: Level with the eyes reads as address between equals. Above reads as looking down on the subject, below as looking up at them. This is the fact most people never record and the one that most reliably reproduces a reference
failure_when_wrong: It must be set together with chin elevation. Low camera plus dropped chin is the jaw-line failure; high camera plus raised chin flattens the face
prompt_phrasing: camera level with the eyes
source: High angle, low angle and eye level as the named positions; the stated conventions are that a high angle can make a subject look small or vulnerable, a low angle powerful or threatening, and eye level has little to no psychological effect. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camera_angle, citing Ascher and Pincus, The Filmmaker's Handbook p214. Treat the directions as film-craft convention: no measured effect sizes were obtained, because the candidate experimental papers were behind bot checks or were image-only PDFs

name_vi: Tiêu cự quy đổi 35mm
what_it_controls: Perspective on the face, via the subject distance it forces. It is not the lens that distorts a face, it is standing close - and a short lens is what makes you stand close to fill the frame
failure_when_wrong: A prompt asking for a wide lens and a tight head-and-shoulders crop is asking for an enlarged nose and receding ears. The two instructions are in conflict and the model will satisfy the crop
prompt_phrasing: 85mm equivalent, head and shoulders
source: Perspective changes are caused by distance, not by the lens: two shots from the same distance show identical perspective geometry whatever lens is used. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perspective_distortion. Sourced anchors: about 50mm is the geometrically correct focal length for prints of 35cm and larger, and the median of 3,930 Flickr SLR photographs was 68mm 35mm-equivalent (Cooper, Piazza and Banks 2012, Journal of Vision 12(5):8, https://jov.arvojournals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2192052); 85 to 135mm is the conventional portrait band. Small screens need longer focal lengths for the same fidelity

name_vi: Khoảng cách từ máy đến người
what_it_controls: The actual cause of facial perspective. State it alongside the focal length so the two cannot contradict each other
failure_when_wrong: Omitted, this is the hidden variable behind every complaint that a portrait looks wrong for reasons the person cannot name
prompt_phrasing: camera about two and a half metres from the subject
source: Measured directly by photographing one face simultaneously at 45cm and 135cm through a half-silvered mirror, normalising on interocular separation and modelling the warp from 115 labelled landmarks: the nose reads relatively larger and the ears smaller as distance decreases, and face width-to-height ratio is smaller for closer faces, t(17)=11.16, p<0.001. Observers could not judge the actual distance, so the cue operates implicitly. Bryan, Perona and Adolphs 2012, PLOS ONE, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0045301. Preferred viewing distance is set by picture size rather than by the focal length used, changing only about 20 percent across a 614 percent change in projection distance. Cooper, Piazza and Banks 2012, Journal of Vision 12(5):8, https://jov.arvojournals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2192052
